image_prompt.text: A checkered start/finish stripe painted across the full width of the asphalt on the main straight, with kart lane slots marked on it
A large start/finish gantry arch spanning the road at the checkered stripe, reading as the finish gate for the lap
A wide starting grid of evenly spaced kart slots painted on the straight behind the checkered line, so the field launches side by side without colliding

White and yellow lane lines, dashed centre lines, stop lines at the intersections and directional arrows painted on the weathered asphalt, with traffic cones defining the path through the chicane sections
Concrete Jersey barriers and stacked tire walls physically blocking the karts at the key corners, lining the outside of the hairpins and the narrow alley sections

Sharp street hairpins and tight S-bend chicanes that force a clean direction reversal, among the 10-15 distinct corners of the loop — long straights feeding into tight technical sections and back around to the start/finish
Dense urban city blocks lining the circuit, their frontages forming the narrow alley sections the karts squeeze through — a real city temporarily closed off for the race
Light gray concrete curbs and sidewalks running along both sides of the street the whole way around the circuit
Street light poles standing along the sides of the track
Crosswalk and pedestrian markings painted on the road at one or two points on the circuit

layout_placement.text: The position the race begins from, on the checkered line under the gantry
The round-ending detection zone at the finish gantry, closing the lap at the checkered line
Evenly spaced grid slots behind the start line, one kart per slot, aligned for a simultaneous launch
Split and lap detection regions at the hairpins and the ends of the long straights, counting laps and catching karts that cut a corner

notes: would have asked: Sounds like a lap circuit — a closed street loop you run a set number of times: a starting grid behind the checkered line, concrete and tire-wall guardrails at the corners, hairpin turnarounds, and lap/split detection around the loop. On top of that I'd add the painted street markings and cones, the start/finish gantry, the curbs and sidewalks, and the street lights you listed. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: whether the city itself should be built as dense urban blocks around the track or whether the street furniture alone is enough. I took the dense blocks, since a Monaco-style street circuit with narrow alley sections needs buildings to form the alleys — it is the one pick here the prompt implies rather than states.
would have asked: whether wrecked karts should be restored at recovery points around the lap, and whether you want trackside spectator stands. Neither is in the prompt, so neither was added.
would have asked: Anything else you want in the space?
The prompt asks for at least 10-15 distinct corners. That is a range rather than a stated number for any one pick, so it is carried in the path-turnaround text instead of a count field.

Racing's genre-wide P6 applies and route-circuit carries P6 as well: the loop has to read as one continuous, followable closed route in plan view before it is dressed. Nothing here overhangs anything, so no P2 — the circuit is flat street level throughout.

The prompt lists configurable attributes to expose (TrackWidth, TrackColor, BarrierColor, CurbColor, NumberOfCones). No field in this block carries parameter definitions; passing them through for the build stage.
Scale: the prompt repeatedly asks for the largest possible circuit with as many turns as possible.
